title: Repeatable top five
brief: A shortlist that names the same five rows every time you ask for it, with equal prices settled the same way.
instructions: Return the five greatest catalog prices. Equal prices are broken by ascending product identity. Return fewer rows only when the data holds fewer than five products.
Return only the declared columns, in their declared order and exact SQL types, and follow the stated ordering contract. NULL placement is declared, not assumed.
starterExplanation: The starter reads product_id and unit_price out of products. It runs. It does not answer the question.

hints.text: A limit without a total order returns whichever rows the engine finds convenient.
Order by price descending, then by identity ascending, and only then take five.
Products 3 and 10002 both cost 888.88, so the tie must resolve the same way twice.

dataClaims.sql: SELECT count(*)::VARCHAR FROM products WHERE unit_price = 888.88 AND product_id IN (3, 10002)
